about: The gospel of the Second Sunday of Advent. John the Baptist, already in prison, sends to ask whether this is He. The answer is not a claim but a list of what can be seen, and it ends with a word about John himself.

seg.tr: At that time, when John heard in prison of the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples and asked Him:
Are You the One who is to come, or should we look for another?
Jesus answered them: Go and report to John what you have heard and seen.
The blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead rise, and the Gospel is preached to the poor; blessed is the one who does not stumble because of Me.
As they went away, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: What did you go out into the desert to see? A reed shaken by the wind?

ex.w061: Latin “abeúntibus illis” expresses a whole clause: “when they were going away”.

seg.tr: What then did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft garments?
Behold, those who wear soft garments live in royal houses.
What then did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
For this is the one of whom it is written: Behold, I send My messenger before Your face, who will prepare Your way before You.
